question: Introduction
answer:
During my field observations at UCSB, I thought love would mostly be found in romantic relationships. But after spending time watching students on campus, I noticed that love often appeared in quieter and more ordinary ways. I saw students helping each other study, listening carefully during conversations, promoting campus activities, and spending time together in supportive ways. These small moments of connection made people feel like they belonged and like they were part of the community, which was important in everyday campus life.
Many of these observations connected to ideas from the Unit 2 readings. In “Love Is Medicine for Fear,” Arthur C. Brooks explains that love and connection can reduce fear and loneliness by helping people feel emotionally supported (Brooks). Emily Esfahani Smith also argues in “The Secret to Love is Just Kindness” that relationships are strengthened through small acts of attention and care rather than dramatic gestures.
Through these observations, I began to understand that love at UCSB is not only romantic. Instead, it often functions as quiet daily care that helps students feel connected, supported, and less isolated in a stressful academic environment.
